ownDerivation:
Loop `fgetc(in1)!=EOF && fgetc(in2)!=EOF` stops either (A) in1 at EOF, in2 never read (short-circuit, in2 sits at the start of its remaining rows), or (B) in1 consumed one char of its next row and in2 is at EOF. So only case B needs one char given back, and only to in1; the official unconditional fseek(-1) on both files steps an EOF/unread file back onto the last '
' and emits a blank line. Fix: `if(!feof(in1)) fseek(in1,-1,SEEK_CUR);` (fseek clears EOF so feof is only true in case A).
tested: clang, BINARY mode (_set_fmode(_O_BINARY)); Windows text-mode ftell/fseek fail (fseek(-1) returns -1), so binary is required. Note that text-mode failure already hits the official in-loop fseek calls, not just the fix.

solution.note: 20000 random differential cases (0-4 lines per file, 1-5 sorted ints per line, all length relations) vs a line-wise reference merge: 0 mismatches. Exam example reproduced exactly (modulo the official trailing space before newline).

outside the stated spec (every line, including the last, ends with newline). Not a defect of the fix: the official rows_merge/next_number already loops forever on such input (fgetc gives EOF, fscanf fails, ch never '
'); with in1 longer and the unterminated row in the copied remainder, fixed code copies it raw correctly. CRLF input in binary mode also hangs the official loop (ch becomes ''); out of spec.
